issues.legal_issue: The statutory review of transfers of protected tribal agricultural land is not limited to transfers in favour of persons outside the protected tribes.
material_facts: The land belonged to agricultural landowners who were members of a protected tribe and was transferred to the appellant, who also claimed membership in a protected tribe.
The transfers occurred during the period covered by the statutory review scheme.
The appellant did not provide the prescribed information about the transfers within the required period, and the revenue authority began an inquiry.
issues.conclusion: The statutory review scheme can apply to a transfer between members of protected tribes; the revenue authority may inquire whether the transfer defrauded the original tribal owner of a legitimate right.
issues.legal_principle: The plain and unambiguous language of Section 170-B(1)–(3) of the Madhya Pradesh Land Revenue Code, 1959, covers the specified transfers without excluding transfers between members of protected tribes. Section 170-B(3) directs the inquiry to whether the original tribal owner was defrauded of a legitimate right. The distinct, narrower wording of Section 170-B(2-A), added in 1998, does not control the meaning of the provisions enacted in 1980. A statement of objects and reasons may illuminate legislative background and purpose but cannot restrict plain statutory language. Girdhari Lal and Sons v. Balbir Nath Mathur supports giving effect to plain words, subject to the recognised limits where that reading causes injustice, absurdity, or invalidity. Dhirendra Nath Sharma v. State of Madhya Pradesh and Atmaram v. State of M.P. are discussed regarding the operation of the statutory inquiry and the presumption arising from failure to report.

rule.if: land_transfer_review_proceeding and protected_tribal_transferor and protected_tribal_possessor and transfer_within_review_period

predicates.land_transfer_review_proceeding: The matter concerns a statutory review of a transfer of agricultural land formerly belonging to a protected tribal landowner.
predicates.protected_tribal_transferor: The person who transferred the land was a member of a protected tribe.
predicates.protected_tribal_possessor: The person in possession of the land was also a member of a protected tribe.
predicates.transfer_within_review_period: The transfer occurred during the period covered by the statutory review scheme.

issues.definition: When a covered land-transfer review concerns a transfer from a protected tribal landowner to a protected tribal possessor during the review period, the review scheme covers that transfer.

issues.legal_issue: Failure to provide prescribed information about a covered land transfer creates a rebuttable presumption but does not itself permit reversion without an inquiry.
material_facts: The appellant did not provide the prescribed information about the transfers within the required period.
The revenue authority initiated proceedings and issued a show-cause notice, but the appellant challenged the notice rather than participating in the inquiry.
issues.conclusion: Failure to provide the information raises a rebuttable presumption of possession without lawful authority; an inquiry under the statutory scheme is still required before an order divesting the possessor of the land.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 170-B(2) and (3) of the Madhya Pradesh Land Revenue Code, 1959, failure to report raises a presumption that is not conclusive and must be considered in the inquiry. Dhirendra Nath Sharma v. State of Madhya Pradesh held that the inquiry requirement prevents automatic divestment and addresses constitutional concerns about deprivation without an inquiry; Atmaram v. State of M.P. further explained that interpretation.

predicates.land_transfer_review_proceeding: The matter concerns a statutory inquiry into possession of land transferred from a protected tribal landowner.
predicates.possessor_failed_to_report_transfer: The person in possession did not provide the prescribed information about the transfer within the required period.

issues.definition: In a statutory land-transfer review, a possessor's failure to report the transfer creates a rebuttable presumption, while reversion requires an inquiry.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge to a show-cause notice initiating the statutory inquiry is premature when the recipient has not participated in that inquiry.
material_facts: The revenue authority issued the appellant a show-cause notice to begin proceedings under the statutory review scheme.
The appellant filed a writ petition challenging the notice instead of first responding and participating in the inquiry.
The High Court rejected the challenge.
issues.conclusion: The show-cause notice was not without jurisdiction, and the appellant's writ petition was premature; the appellant should have participated in the inquiry.
issues.legal_principle: Section 170-B(3) authorises an inquiry into covered land transfers. Where the statutory authority has initiated that inquiry by issuing a show-cause notice, a challenge made before the recipient participates in the inquiry is premature. The Court accordingly upheld the High Court's rejection of the writ petition.

predicates.challenge_to_show_cause_notice: The proceeding is a challenge to a notice calling on a person to respond to a proposed statutory inquiry.
predicates.statutory_land_transfer_inquiry_started: The competent authority has initiated an inquiry into a covered land transfer.
predicates.recipient_has_not_participated: The recipient challenged the notice without first responding to or participating in the inquiry.

issues.definition: A recipient who challenges a show-cause notice before participating in an inquiry already initiated by the competent authority brings a premature challenge to a notice that is not without jurisdiction.
